read_me_first.headline: The market is in Stage 2 (Advancing): the mark-up phase of the cycle, 30 weeks in. A change of stage is in progress but not yet confirmed. SPY and QQQ are at the canon's market-top reading on distribution days.
because: Stage 2 means advancing: price above a rising 30-week average. The last completed week closed 0.29% above the 30-week average (752.22), and that average has risen 1.47% over four weeks.
Distribution days (down closes on heavier volume) in the last 25 sessions: SPY 9, QQQ 9. O'Neil's canon reads 4 or more as a market top.
QQQ is in Stage 3 (Topping), which disagrees with SPY.
Of 1678 single names on AQE's panel, 40.1% are in Stage 2 (four weeks ago 35.1%) and 26.3% are in Stage 4 (four weeks ago 34.7%): the single names agree with the index.
Sectors: Stage 2 (Advancing): XLB, XLE, XLF, XLP, XLV, XLY; Stage 3 (Topping): XLI, XLK, XLRE; Stage 4 (Declining): XLC, XLU.
read_me_first.so_what: Stage 2 is the only stage in which the long-only playbook is designed to work. Doctrine: buy breakouts and pullbacks that hold the 30-week average.
watch_for: SPY: the week still forming reads Stage 3 (Topping).
A weekly close below the 30-week average (about 752.22) is the first sign of a top.
SPY has 9 distribution days in 25 sessions, at or above the canon's top signal (4).
QQQ has 9 distribution days in 25 sessions, at or above the canon's top signal (4).
caveats: Breadth counts every single name on AQE's own weekly panel (aqe_panel_equities), not the whole US market.

source: Weinstein four-stage analysis on weekly bars (src/stages/spec.py)

distribution_days.note: any down close on heavier volume counts (the canon sets no minimum decline); stall days are not counted (the canon gives no number for 'negligible progress')
